question_en:
This old photograph, preserved in the local archives, is kept together with historical records of local buildings. To complete the exhibition board record, please answer the following questions:

1. What are the USGS station number and official station name for this station? What is the name and purpose of the equipment shown in the image?
2. What were the station location and observation method for the three periods: 1928–1959, 1959–1960, and 1960–1962?
3. What gage datum was used during 1960–1962, and what gage datum was adopted later for the long term? What is the difference between them? What are the Altitude of gage/land surface and vertical datum currently listed on the station page?

Response format: Please answer in separate points numbered (1)–(3). Each point should only address the corresponding sub-question and provide all information required by that question. For point 2, use a table with columns "Period," "Station Location," and "Observation Method." For the other two points, provide text answers.
answer:
(1) USGS station number: 05054000; Official station name: Red River of the North at Fargo, North Dakota; Equipment: Price electric current meters; Purpose: Measure water flow velocity using a vertical-axis cup rotor and calculate discharge in combination with the flow cross-section.

(2)

| Period | Station Location | Observation Method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1928-08-01—1959-04-12 | Near the Fargo Municipal Water Plant, approximately 1.0 mile downstream of the later station site; upstream of Island Park Dam, river mile 452.1 | Daily manual reading of staff gage |
| 1959-04-13—1960-09-30 | Concrete stilling well on the downstream side of the Interstate 94 bridge, located 2.0 miles upstream of the previous station site | Automatic continuous recorder |
| 1960-10-01—1962-09-30 | Fargo Municipal Water Plant | continuous recorder |

(3) Gage datum for 1960–1962: 867.4 ft NGVD 1929; Gage datum adopted later for the long term: 861.8 ft NGVD 1929; Difference: 5.6 ft, with the former being higher; Current Altitude of gage/land surface: 862.7 ft; Vertical datum: NAVD88.

# Detailed Simulated Search Trajectory · 8-2-E03

## Step 01 · Decompose the question and establish fields to verify

**Action:** Record required fields for each sub-question according to the current prompt; first identify the bridge entity from the input image, then map each answer field to a verifiable source.

**Evidence Observation:**

This old photograph, preserved in the local archives, is kept together with historical records of local buildings. To complete the exhibition board record, please answer the following questions:

1. What are the USGS station number and official station name for this station? What is the name and purpose of the equipment shown in the image?
2. What were the station location and observation method for the three periods: 1928–1959, 1959–1960, and 1960–1962?
3. What gage datum was used during 1960–1962, and what gage datum was adopted later for the long term? What is the difference between them? What are the Altitude of gage/land surface and vertical datum currently listed on the station page?

Response format: Please answer in separate points numbered (1)–(3). Each point should only address the corresponding sub-question and provide all information required by that question. For point 2, use a table with columns "Period," "Station Location," and "Observation Method." For the other two points, provide text answers.

**Evidence Links:**

Current prompt and input attachments; this step does not introduce external web pages.

**Result of this step:** The search path expands according to these sub-questions; the image serves as the entry point for objects, while numbers, dates, statistics, and status must be read from corresponding records.

## Step 02 · Locate the original plate based on instrument morphology

**Action:** Example query: USGS Price electric current meters Plate I Water Supply Paper64; compare the instrument stand and cup rotor layout.

**Evidence Observation:**

The title of Plate I in WSP64 is Price electric current meters, providing the equipment name and an anchor to the original image. It can identify the equipment category but does not alone prove which station the photograph belongs to.

**Evidence Links:**

https://pubs.usgs.gov/wsp/0064/report.pdf

**Result of this step:** The equipment candidate is the Price electric current meter.

## Step 03 · Trace from local station history images to the station

**Action:** Search for the USGS Red River of the North at Fargo 110 years article, then cross-check its historical images and station number.

**Evidence Observation:**

Saved extraction records link the same image to Fargo 05054000. Requests to the webpage from the command line returned 403, so only factual excerpts read online are retained; do not claim to have the complete original HTML. The equipment image being placed beside local building records does not mean the building itself is the instrument model.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.usgs.gov/centers/dakota-water-science-center/red-river-north-fargo-north-dakota-110-years

**Result of this step:** The station number for the first question converges to 05054000.

## Step 04 · Verify the official station name and equipment function

**Action:** Open the current USGS monitoring-location page and combine it with WSP equipment descriptions.

**Evidence Observation:**

Official station name: Red River of the North at Fargo, North Dakota. The Price meter measures water velocity with a vertical-axis cup rotor; that velocity is then combined with cross-section measurements to calculate discharge. It is not a staff gage that directly measures water level.

**Evidence Links:**

https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/USGS-05054000/
https://pubs.usgs.gov/wsp/0064/report.pdf

**Result of this step:** The station name and purpose for the first question are completed.

## Step 05 · Distinguish between current meter and water level observation methods

**Action:** Read USGS gage height descriptions to establish the three fields: gage height, gage datum, and discharge.

**Evidence Observation:**

Flow velocity, discharge, water level, and the zero point of the gage are not the same physical quantities; the second item in the question regarding staff gage/continuous recorder refers to the station's water level observation method. One should not fill in the Price instrument as the observation method for all periods simply because the old photograph shows a current meter.

**Evidence Links:**

https://waterdata.usgs.gov/blog/gage_height/

**Result of this step:** Use the correct observation fields for the station history table.

## Step 06 · Obtain official water level station history attachments

**Action:** Locate the station 05054000 gage height history write-up and the saved direct PDF.

**Evidence Observation:**

The official station history lists station location, method, and datum segment by segment with precise start and end dates; this is the primary evidence for the three-period table. The 110-year anniversary article provides an overview of station relocations but does not replace the boundaries of the official segmented records.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.usgs.gov/media/files/station-05054000-gage-height-history-write
https://www.usgs.gov/centers/dakota-water-science-center/red-river-north-fargo-north-dakota-110-years

**Result of this step:** Fill in the three rows sequentially according to the station history dates.

## Step 07 · Read the 1928 to 1959 segment

**Action:** Locate August 1, 1928 to April 12, 1959, and verify location, relative distance, and reading method item by item.

**Evidence Observation:**

Near the Fargo Municipal Water Plant, approximately 1.0 mile downstream of the later station site, with daily manual reading of the staff gage; WSP1308 supplements this with upstream of Island Park Dam, river mile 452.1. Retain the distance reference to the "later station site" to avoid confusing the upstream/downstream relationships of each segment.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.usgs.gov/media/files/station-05054000-gage-height-history-write
https://pubs.usgs.gov/wsp/1308/report.pdf

**Result of this step:** The first period is completely filled in as 1928-08-01—1959-04-12.

## Step 08 · Read the 1959 to 1960 segment

**Action:** Locate April 13, 1959 to September 30, 1960, and verify the bridge and well structure.

**Evidence Observation:**

Concrete stilling well on the downstream side of the Interstate 94 bridge, located 2.0 miles upstream of the previous station site, using a continuous recorder. The official segmented start date is not the August 12 data collection narrative described in the anniversary article; the final table follows the official station history.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.usgs.gov/media/files/station-05054000-gage-height-history-write
https://www.usgs.gov/centers/dakota-water-science-center/red-river-north-fargo-north-dakota-110-years

**Result of this step:** The second period is filled in as 1959-04-13—1960-09-30 with automatic continuous recording.

## Step 09 · Read the 1960 to 1962 segment

**Action:** Locate October 1, 1960 to September 30, 1962.

**Evidence Observation:**

The station location returned to the Fargo Municipal Water Plant, using a continuous recorder. The anniversary text mentions a physical relocation on 1960-06-22; the date of the relocation narrative cannot directly replace the start point of this statistical segment in the observation history.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.usgs.gov/media/files/station-05054000-gage-height-history-write
https://www.usgs.gov/centers/dakota-water-science-center/red-river-north-fargo-north-dakota-110-years

**Result of this step:** Fill in the table for the third period according to the official interval.

## Step 10 · Verify the two historical gage datums

**Action:** Cross-read the official station history and the 05054000 section of the 1980 Water Data Report.

**Evidence Observation:**

1960–1962 is 867.4 ft NGVD 1929; the datum adopted later for the long term is 861.8 ft NGVD 1929. The 1980 report directly states that 1960–1962 was at the current station but with a datum 5.6 ft higher, providing an independent cross-check.

**Evidence Links:**

https://www.usgs.gov/media/files/station-05054000-gage-height-history-write
https://pubs.usgs.gov/wdr/1980/mn-80-1/report.pdf

**Result of this step:** The two historical values and the common datum for the third question are determined.

## Step 11 · Calculate the difference under the same datum

**Action:** Before calculating, check that units are all in ft and the datum is NGVD 1929 for both.

**Evidence Observation:**

867.4 − 861.8 = 5.6 ft, with the former being higher; this is the elevation difference of the water level zero point, not the amount of river surface drop. Do not mix meter values or different vertical datums into the calculation.

**Evidence Links:**

https://pubs.usgs.gov/wdr/1980/mn-80-1/report.pdf
https://www.usgs.gov/media/files/station-05054000-gage-height-history-write

**Result of this step:** The difference and direction can be reported directly.

## Step 12 · Read precise fields from the current station page

**Action:** Locate Altitude of gage/land surface and Altitude datum on the current USGS saved page.

**Evidence Observation:**

Field value 862.7 feet, vertical datum North American Vertical Datum of 1988 (NAVD88); this is not the same-named historical zero point marked as 861.8 ft NGVD 29 on the page. One cannot derive ground uplift or subsidence without datum conversion by subtracting 861.8 from 862.7.

**Evidence Links:**

https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/USGS-05054000/

**Result of this step:** The current values 862.7 ft and NAVD88 are listed independently.

## Step 13 · Check the final table and numerical interpretation

**Action:** Compare the station, instrument, and datum columns for the three periods to confirm that plate dates were not inserted into the station history timeline.

**Evidence Observation:**

Old images identify the equipment, Fargo station history identifies the station and relocations; the three time periods follow the write-up, historical zero point differences are subtracted under the same datum, and current Altitude is retained under its original field name. Evidence can be combined, but fields cannot be renamed across categories.

**Evidence Links:**

https://pubs.usgs.gov/wsp/0064/report.pdf
https://www.usgs.gov/media/files/station-05054000-gage-height-history-write
https://pubs.usgs.gov/wdr/1980/mn-80-1/report.pdf
https://waterdata.usgs.gov/monitoring-location/USGS-05054000/

**Result of this step:** Completion of image captions, history table, and elevation explanation for the three questions.

## Step 14 · Check evidence dependencies and answer boundaries

**Action:** Connect the obtained bridge entities in order of dependency, and check each question for number mismatches, changes in time scope, or presenting inferences as facts.

**Evidence Observation:**

Dependency chain: Old instrument plate → Price current meter → Fargo station history 05054000 → Station location/observation by period → Historical zero point difference under the same datum → Current station fields and NAVD88.

Limits to preserve: The relocation dates described in the anniversary article differ from the period boundaries in the official station history. The value 862.7 belongs to the Altitude field and uses NAVD88; it cannot be directly compared by subtraction with an elevation referenced to NGVD 29.

**Evidence Links:**

Current prompt and input attachments; this step does not introduce external web pages.

**Result of this step:** Each field adopts the evidence directly corresponding to it above; organize the confirmed conclusions according to the numbering, table, and units specified in the prompt.

## Step 15 · final_answer

**Action:** Submit the answer according to the fields required by the current prompt.

**Evidence Observation:** Cross-checks of objects, sources, and corresponding versions are completed, retaining information that could not be confirmed as noted above.

**Result of this step:**

(1) USGS station number: 05054000; Official station name: Red River of the North at Fargo, North Dakota; Equipment: Price electric current meters; Purpose: Measure water flow velocity using a vertical-axis cup rotor and calculate discharge in combination with the flow cross-section.

（2）

| Period | Station Location | Observation Method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1928-08-01—1959-04-12 | Near the Fargo Municipal Water Plant, approximately 1.0 mile downstream of the later station site; upstream of Island Park Dam, river mile 452.1 | Daily manual reading of staff gage |
| 1959-04-13—1960-09-30 | Concrete stilling well on the downstream side of the Interstate 94 bridge, located 2.0 miles upstream of the previous station site | Automatic continuous recorder |
| 1960-10-01—1962-09-30 | Fargo Municipal Water Plant | continuous recorder |

(3) Gage datum for 1960–1962: 867.4 ft NGVD 1929; Gage datum adopted later for the long term: 861.8 ft NGVD 1929; Difference: 5.6 ft, with the former being higher; Current Altitude of gage/land surface: 862.7 ft; Vertical datum: NAVD88.
